stories.excerpt: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 5 – The Pharmacy and Poisons Board (PPB) has cautioned Kenyans against misusing cetirizine tablets for vaginal tightening or drying, warning that the practice circulating on social media could expose users to health complications. In a safety alert, the Board dismissed claims suggesting that cetirizine, an antihistamine used to relieve allergic conditions, can be used for vaginal purposes. The regulator said there was no established scientific evidence supporting the claims and emphasised that cetirizine is not approved for vaginal use. stories.excerpt: The World Health Organization (WHO) has warned that funding cuts and declining international support could reverse progress against neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), despite significant gains in prevention and treatment globally. The WHO’s 2026 Global Report on Neglected Tropical Diseases shows that 63 countries had eliminated at least one NTD by June 2026, up from 42 at the end of 2020. In a press release, WHO says that the number of people requiring interventions for NTDs fell to 1.41 billion in 2024, representing a 36 per cent decline since 2010 and a 19 per cent reduction since 2020. Cases of sleeping sickness have dropped by 98 per cent since 1999, while guinea worm disease recorded only 10 human cases in 2025. However, the report warns that overall resources available for NTD programmes remain 30 per cent below pre-COVID-19 levels, with some programmes facing near-total loss of dedicated funding. The discovery was made using the Large Hadron Collider, which smashes protons together to produce particles that scientists can study. Researchers focused on beauty particles, short-lived particles created in these collisions. They found evidence of an extremely rare process in which one of these particles transforms into other particles, something predicted to happen just once in every 10 billion cases. This incredibly small scale is what scientists call the 'zeptoverse': an unexplored frontier of the subatomic world, where researchers hope to discover new fundamental particles. stories.excerpt: Dar es Salaam. Tanzania’s pass rate in the 2026 Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) has risen to 85.22 percent, with 970,876 candidates passing out of the 1,139,273 who sat the examination. Announcing the results on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, National Examinations Council of Tanzania (NECTA) Executive Secretary, Prof Said Mohamed, said the candidates had obtained Grades A, B and C. The latest results represent a 3.42 percentage-point increase in the overall pass rate from 81.80 percent recorded in 2025. In terms of performance quality, 429,667 candidates, equivalent to 37.72 percent, secured Grades A and B, representing a 0.82 percentage-point improvement compared with the previous year. The improvement points to continued progress in primary school examination performance, although questions remain about the factors driving the gains and the extent to which they translate into better learning outcomes.
